projects.readme:
# PDRides — Full-Stack Ride-Sharing Application

**Public-Demand Ride-share Made Easy**

PDRides is a community ride-sharing web application that connects passengers and drivers through a browser interface and messaging integrations. The project brings together ride discovery, driver ride offers, seat booking, route planning, estimated fares, account settings, and advertising configuration. Its product goal is a platform with no platform fees for passengers or drivers.

![PDRides project screenshot showing the home page and messaging entry points](docs/images/pdrides-home.png)

*Actual project home page captured locally. Marketing statements displayed in the interface are product copy, not independently verified usage or service guarantees.*

[Source code](https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-FullStack-PDRides/issues)

## Project overview

Drivers can publish trips with pickup and destination details, timing, available seats, and a contribution amount. Passengers can discover rides and use booking flows. Map services supply location search, routing, distance, and fare estimates. WhatsApp supports messaging and phone verification; Telegram webhook and bot service modules are also included. MongoDB stores users, rides, conversations, and advertisements.

This repository is an application prototype with implemented backend routes and frontend screens. Messaging requires configured provider accounts, and the instant booking flow currently assigns a mock driver. A screenshot or a successful server start does not establish that all integrations are working in production.

## Features and implementation

| Area | Included in the codebase |
| --- | --- |
| Ride discovery | Browse rides, filter by trip details, view shared ride pages, and see seat availability |
| Driver tools | Publish and manage ride offers with vehicle/profile information |
| Passenger tools | Book seats, cancel bookings, and review ride history |
| Maps | Leaflet interface, OpenStreetMap tiles, Nominatim location lookup, and OSRM routing |
| Fare estimates | Distance/time calculations, ride-type pricing, and detailed fare breakdowns |
| Accounts | WhatsApp OTP flows, registration, sessions, profile and driver settings |
| Preferences | Favorite routes, recent searches, privacy and notification settings |
| Messaging | WhatsApp Cloud API service/webhook and Telegram bot service/webhook |
| Advertising | Ad models, API routes, placement configuration, geographic targeting, and fallback content |
| Maintenance | Scheduled ride expiration and completion tasks; application/database health routes |

## Technology

- **Frontend:** HTML, CSS, browser JavaScript, and Leaflet.
- **Backend:** Node.js with ECMAScript modules and Express 4.
- **Persistence:** MongoDB, Mongoose 8, and the MongoDB Node.js driver 7.
- **Integrations:** WhatsApp Cloud API, Telegram Bot API, Nominatim, and OSRM.
- **Utilities:** Axios, dotenv, node-cron, and nodemon for development.

## Local setup

### Prerequisites

- Node.js **20.19 or newer**, matching the minimum required by the declared MongoDB 7 driver dependency.
- npm and a reachable MongoDB instance, locally or hosted.
- A Meta WhatsApp Cloud API application for WhatsApp delivery and OTP testing.
- A Telegram bot token if testing Telegram integration.

### Install and configure

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides.git
cd FullStack-PDRides
npm install
```

Copy the environment template:

```powershell
# PowerShell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` with your own configuration. Use the same port in `PORT` and `WEB_APP_URL`; the template currently has different values. A consistent local example is:

```dotenv
PORT=3000
NODE_ENV=development
APP_NAME=PDRides
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/pdrides
WEB_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID=your_phone_number_id
WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_access_token
WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN=your_verification_token
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your_bot_token
TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_webhook_secret
MAX_RIDE_RESULTS=5
```

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PORT` | HTTP port; the server falls back to `3002` when unset |
| `MONGODB_URI` | Database connection; `MONGO_URI` and `MONGODB_URL` are fallback aliases |
| `MONGODB_DATABASE` | Optional database name; defaults to `pdrides` |
| `WEB_APP_URL` | Base URL used for links sent in messages |
| `APP_NAME` | Optional display name in server/health output |
| `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` | Your Meta WhatsApp phone-number resource ID |
| `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Credential for WhatsApp message delivery |
| `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` | Value used during webhook verification |
| `WHATSAPP_API_VERSION` | Optional Graph API version override used by the WhatsApp service |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Telegram bot credential |
| `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Telegram webhook configuration secret |
| `MAX_RIDE_RESULTS` | Ride-result configuration from the environment template |

The template also contains `MAPBOX_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTESERVICE_KEY`; the current map service uses Nominatim and OSRM directly. Keep `.env` private and replace the example phone-number ID with your own.

Some integration modules read environment variables during module initialization. If credentials from `.env` are not picked up with `npm start`, preload the file before importing the app:

```bash
node --env-file=.env src/index.js
```

### Run

```bash
npm run dev
# or
npm start
```

The backend connects to MongoDB before opening its HTTP listener. With the configuration above, visit `http://localhost:3000/`.

## Screens and routes

| URL | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Home page |
| `/map` | Interactive map and trip planning |
| `/register` | Registration |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/browse-all-rides` | Ride discovery |
| `/my-rides` | Personal rides |
| `/ride/:id` | Shareable ride details |
| `/settings` | Account and preferences |
| `/ads-config` | Advertising configuration interface |
| `/help-center` | Help content |
| `/contact-us` | Contact page |
| `/privacy-policy` | Privacy policy |
| `/terms-of-service` | Terms of service |

The static HTML files are also present at the repository root. Opening only those files does not supply the API or database functionality.

## API overview

| Endpoint or group | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | Application liveness |
| `GET /api/health`, `GET /api/ping` | Database-aware health and connectivity |
| `/api/auth/*` | OTP requests, verification, registration, and session operations |
| `/api/user/*` | Profile, vehicle details, preferences, and history |
| `/api/users/me/*` | Unified current-user profile and preferences routes |
| `GET /api/rides`, `POST /api/rides` | Search and create ride offers |
| `/api/rides/:id/*` | Ride booking, cancellation, completion, and status operations |
| `GET /api/fare` | Fare estimates for pickup/destination locations |
| `POST /api/ride/book` | Prototype instant booking with a mock driver |
| `GET /api/route` | Route details |
| `GET /api/autocomplete`, `GET /api/reverse-geocode` | Location lookup |
| `/api/ads*` | Advertisement management and delivery routes |
| `/webhook` | WhatsApp verification and incoming events |
| `/telegram-webhook` | Telegram incoming events |

Consult [the app entry point](src/index.js) and [route modules](src/routes) for request fields and authorization behavior. Some ride and location routes are defined in the entry point before the unified API router; Express handles the first matching route, so overlapping handlers need to be considered when extending the API.

## Messaging setup

**WhatsApp:** Configure your own Meta credentials and verification token, expose the app through an HTTPS URL, and configure the callback at `/webhook`. Subscribe the provider application to the events needed by the webhook handlers. OTP and outgoing-message flows require working provider credentials.

**Telegram:** Configure your own bot token and webhook settings. [set-telegram-webhook.js](set-telegram-webhook.js) is the repository's setup helper; inspect its configuration before running it against a bot. The source includes both Telegram and WhatsApp integrations, but their presence does not confirm a deployed bot is online.

## Repository layout

```text
FullStack-PDRides/
├── index.html                 # Landing page
├── map-view.html              # Map and trip planning UI
├── browse-rides.html           # Ride discovery UI
├── my-rides.html               # Personal ride UI
├── ride-details.html           # Shared ride UI
├── login.html / register.html  # Account entry screens
├── settings.html               # User preferences
├── ads-config.html             # Advertising UI
├── css/                        # Screen styles
├── src/
│   ├── index.js                # Express app, routes, startup
│   ├── middleware/             # Authentication helpers
│   ├── models/                 # User, Ride, Conversation, Ad
│   ├── routes/                 # Auth, user, API, messaging, ads
│   └── services/               # Database, rides, maps, messaging, scheduling
├── ads-config/                 # Placement, targeting, unit and fallback JSON
├── ads-system/                 # Ad loader and developer configuration
├── docs/images/                # README project screenshot
├── test-*.js / test-*.json      # Manual integration scripts and sample payloads
├── .env.example                # Environment template
└── package.json                # Dependencies and commands
```

## Verification and current limitations

`npm test` is currently a placeholder that exits with an error; there is no automated test suite configured. The `test-*.js` scripts and `test-bot.html` are manual integration aids. Review their endpoints and payloads before running them, since some can send messages or modify records.

For a configured local instance:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl http://localhost:3000/api/health
```

Then exercise registration, an offered ride, ride discovery, booking/cancellation, and the messaging callbacks with test accounts.

Before production use, review authentication and authorization across all routes, OTP handling, CORS, input validation, provider webhook verification, and static file exposure. The app currently serves the repository root as static content, includes permissive demo CORS, and contains mock instant-booking behavior. These are implementation limitations rather than production service guarantees. Advertised live tracking, driver verification, reviews, and user-count claims should be validated against a complete deployed flow before being represented as operational capabilities.

## Contributing

Open an issue with reproduction steps or a proposed improvement. For code changes, describe the affected flow, configuration needs, and how it was verified. Do not include credentials, personal ride data, or production message payloads.

`package.json` declares MIT, but this repository currently has no standalone `LICENSE` file. Confirm the intended license terms with the repository owner before relying on a license grant.

# GenAI Game Industry Research Agents

![CrewAI project overview: researcher, writer, and Markdown article](docs/project-overview.svg)

A Python experiment that coordinates a **Senior Researcher** and a **Writer** with CrewAI. The crew searches the web through Serper, investigates technology trends in the games industry, and turns its findings into a Markdown article.

## Project summary

This repository demonstrates role-based agents, tool use, sequential tasks, memory, and caching in one readable script. It is a learning prototype rather than a deployed application. The project image above is an architecture illustration, not a screenshot of a user interface.

## How the workflow works

1. The researcher searches for games-industry trends and evaluates benefits, market opportunities, and risks.
2. The research task requests a three-paragraph report.
3. The writer runs after the researcher in a sequential crew and writes an accessible four-paragraph article.
4. CrewAI saves the article to `new-blog-post2.md`, and the script prints the final result.

| Component | Configuration in the script |
| --- | --- |
| Senior Researcher | Web search, verbose logging, memory, delegation enabled |
| Writer | Web search, verbose logging, memory, delegation disabled |
| Search tool | `SerperDevTool` |
| Execution | `Process.sequential` |
| Crew settings | Memory and caching enabled; `max_rpm=100` |
| Output | Markdown file plus terminal output |

## Repository contents

```text
app.py                       Agent definitions, tasks, crew, and execution
requirements.txt             Python dependencies (unpinned)
.env.example                 Placeholder environment variable names
.gitignore                   Excludes secrets, caches, and generated output
new-blog-post.md              Historical sample output from a different topic
README.md                    Project documentation
docs/project-overview.svg    Project architecture image
```

The historical `new-blog-post.md` discusses a different industry and contains unverified claims. It is retained as an existing artifact and is not representative of the current games-industry prompts or a validated research result.

## Setup

Use a Python version supported by your installed CrewAI release. See the [official CrewAI installation guide](https://docs.crewai.com/en/installation) for current requirements.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents.git
cd GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

On macOS/Linux, activate the environment with `source .venv/bin/activate`.

### Credentials

The script reads two environment variables. Set them in the terminal where you run the project:

```powershell
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY"
$env:SERPER_API_KEY = "YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
python app.py
```

For macOS/Linux:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY"
export SERPER_API_KEY="YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
python app.py
```

`.env.example` is a reference only: the script does not automatically load `.env` files. Never put real credentials in source control. Missing credentials cause a clear error before the crew is constructed. Obtain credentials from [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/) and [Serper](https://serper.dev/). Running the crew makes external API calls and may incur charges.

## Customizing the crew

Edit the agent `role`, `goal`, and `backstory` fields to change responsibilities. Adjust each task's `description` and `expected_output` to control the research scope and article structure. Change `output_file` to choose a different destination.

The `topic` passed to `crew.kickoff()` is currently not referenced through a `{topic}` placeholder in the task descriptions. Changing that input alone will not retarget the hardcoded games-industry prompts; edit the prompts as well. The research task's expected output mentions AI trends, while its description covers games-industry trends more broadly.

## Limitations and validation

- This is an older CrewAI example. Dependencies are unpinned, and compatibility with current releases has not been established. Settings such as `share_crew=True` may require review against the installed version.
- No model is explicitly selected in the script; model behavior and access depend on CrewAI configuration and provider defaults.
- Memory may require additional provider configuration and local storage, depending on the installed release.
- Search results and generated claims need human verification. The script does not enforce citations or fact-check its output.
- Verbose logs can contain prompts, research, and generated text. Review the configured sharing and logging behavior before processing private information.
- Publication checks cover Python syntax, repository contents, and credential removal. A live paid API run has not been performed.

## Suggested next steps

Pin and test compatible dependency versions, parameterize the topic in all prompts, add explicit source citations, and make model selection configurable. A CLI and repeatable integration tests would make the prototype easier to maintain.

## References

- [CrewAI source and documentation](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI)
- [CrewAI installation](https://docs.crewai.com/en/installation)
- [Serper](https://serper.dev/)

## License

projects.readme:
# GenAI · LangChat Agent

**A compact Python playground for LangChain chat models, tool schemas, and command-line conversations.**

![LangChat project overview](docs/project-overview.svg)

LangChat explores the building blocks of a generative AI assistant: a chat model, a timezone lookup tool, single-prompt and interactive CLI modes, and an offline fallback. Its small codebase is intended for learning and experimentation.

> **Status:** Educational prototype. The offline fallback works without an API key. The live model path needs message adaptation and a tool execution loop. Document retrieval and RAG are planned extensions, not implemented features.

## Project name

`GenAI-LangChat-Agent` follows **Project Type – Project Name**. GenAI describes the generative chat model, LangChat preserves the project identity, and Agent describes the intended tool-using direction. This project does not train an ML/DL model. RAGBot would imply a retrieval pipeline that is not present in this source.

## Features and implementation

| Component | Current behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Model configuration | ChatOpenAI with temperature zero and a configurable model name |
| Tool schema | `get_time_in_timezone` returns formatted time for an IANA timezone |
| Tool binding | `llm.bind_tools` advertises the timezone tool to the model |
| Offline fallback | Fixed setup message when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is absent |
| Single prompt | CLI `--prompt` argument |
| Interactive CLI | In-memory conversation tuples; `exit` or `quit` ends the session |
| Logging | Loguru events; optional rotating-file configuration helper |
| Tests | One factory-construction smoke test |

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Python CLI] --> B[Load environment and build agent]
    B --> C{API key configured?}
    C -->|No| D[Local fallback message]
    C -->|Yes| E[ChatOpenAI with bound tool schema]
    E -. Message adapter and execution loop needed .-> F[Tool-using conversation]
    G[Timezone tool schema] --> E
```

`build_agent()` returns either a local fallback accepting an input dictionary or a LangChain model runnable. Those paths do not yet share a compatible input/output interface. A prompt template is constructed but is not connected to the runnable. Tool binding supplies a schema; it does not execute the Python tool or return its result to the model.

## Technology

Python 3.10+, LangChain, langchain-openai, python-dotenv, Loguru, Python zoneinfo, and pytest. Runtime requirements are in `requirements.txt`; test requirements are in `test_requirements.txt`. The original `pyproject.toml` has an empty dependencies list, so install using the requirements files.

## Setup

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-LangChat-Agent.git
cd GenAI-LangChat-Agent
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt -r test_requirements.txt
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

On macOS/Linux, activate with `source .venv/bin/activate` and copy with `cp .env.example .env`.

Leave `OPENAI_API_KEY` empty for the offline demo. To develop the live path, configure your own key privately in `.env`. Never commit credentials. Configuring a key does not resolve the incomplete live execution path described below.

## Usage

Run from the repository root after installing dependencies.

### Offline single-prompt demo

With no key configured:

```powershell
python src/agent_cli.py --prompt "What time is it in UTC?"
```

Expected response:

```text
(LLM disabled: set OPENAI_API_KEY to enable the agent.)
```

The fallback does not answer questions or execute tools.

### Interactive mode

```powershell
python src/agent_cli.py --interactive
```

Enter text at `You>`. Type `exit` or `quit` to end. Conversation history lasts only for the process. The live runnable needs interface repairs before it can consume that history correctly.

### Model selection argument

```powershell
python src/agent_cli.py --prompt "Hello" --model YOUR_MODEL_NAME
```

The CLI source defaults to `gpt-4o-mini`; the factory defaults to `gpt-3.5-turbo`. These are source defaults, not model availability guarantees.

### Direct timezone tool

```powershell
python -c "from src.agent import get_time_in_timezone; print(get_time_in_timezone.invoke({'timezone': 'UTC'}))"
```

Examples: `UTC`, `America/New_York`, `Asia/Kolkata`. Accessible IANA timezone data is required. If the operating system lacks it, install the optional `tzdata` package. Invalid names currently raise an exception.

## Tests

```powershell
python -m pytest -q
```

The included test checks factory construction only. It does not validate model output, tool execution, retrieval, or deployment readiness. No API request is needed when the key is absent.

## Project structure

```text
GenAI-LangChat-Agent/
  README.md
  docs/project-overview.svg
  .env.example
  .gitignore
  pyproject.toml
  requirements.txt
  test_requirements.txt
  conftest.py
  src/
    agent.py
    agent_cli.py
    logging_config.py
    tests/test_agent.py
```

## Logging and local data

The CLI logs prompt text through Loguru. Avoid sensitive prompts if logs may be collected. `configure_logging()` defines rotating `agent.log` files and console output, but is not currently called by the CLI. Local environments, caches, credentials, logs, and build artifacts are excluded through `.gitignore`.

## Known limitations

- The CLI passes an `input`/`chat_history` dictionary and expects a dictionary response; the live model runnable needs message input and returns a different response type.
- Tool calls are not dispatched and results are not sent back to the model.
- The prompt template and scratchpad are not wired into execution.
- There is no document ingestion, chunking, embedding model, vector store, retrieval, or citation support.
- There is no web UI, persistent history, authentication, or deployment configuration.
- Dependencies have lower bounds rather than a lock file.
- Error handling, bounded execution, retries, timeouts, and end-to-end tests need development.

## Roadmap toward a RAG bot

1. Normalize executor inputs/outputs and connect the prompt template.
2. Add a bounded model/tool execution loop with tool-result messages.
3. Test execution with fake model responses and explicit offline configuration.
4. Implement document loading, chunking, embeddings, and a vector store.
5. Retrieve relevant chunks and generate answers with document citations.
6. Evaluate retrieval quality and add persistence and deployment controls.

## Contributions and licensing

Focused fixes, tests, and documentation improvements are welcome through issues and pull requests. Keep examples free of private documents and credentials. No license has been selected; public visibility alone does not grant an open-source license.

# GenAI - Multimodal Generation Lab

**Build and explore generative AI across text, images, video, vision, speech, music, and 3D with hands-on PyTorch notebooks.**

![Class-conditional sneaker images generated by the project's diffusion model](assets/project-preview.png)

*Actual saved output from the image diffusion notebook: eight Fashion-MNIST sneaker samples generated from noise.*

This educational project walks through seven generative modeling workflows, from preparing data and implementing an architecture to training, sampling, and inspecting results. It includes a combined master notebook, individual notebooks for focused study, and optional pretrained inference examples. The master notebook also exposes a small `MultiModalHub` dispatcher for calling the trained generators through one interface.

The emphasis is understanding how models learn. These are compact teaching implementations with limited datasets and training budgets. The seven workflows cover different modalities; the project does not train a single jointly aligned multimodal foundation model.

## Notebook guide

| Modality | Notebook | Architecture and objective | Data and output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text | [01_Text_GPT.ipynb](01_Text_GPT.ipynb) | Character-level GPT with causal self-attention and next-token cross-entropy | Tiny Shakespeare → sampled text continuations |
| Image | [02_Image_Diffusion.ipynb](02_Image_Diffusion.ipynb) | Class-conditional UNet DDPM, noise-prediction MSE, classifier-free guidance | Fashion-MNIST → 28 × 28 grayscale garment images |
| Video | [03_Video_FramePrediction.ipynb](03_Video_FramePrediction.ipynb) | ConvLSTM sequence prediction with pixel MSE and teacher forcing | Moving sequences constructed from MNIST → future frames |
| Vision | [04_Vision_MaskedImageModeling.ipynb](04_Vision_MaskedImageModeling.ipynb) | Masked autoencoder with reconstruction loss on hidden patches | CIFAR-10 → reconstructed missing image regions |
| Speech | [05_Speech_TextToSpeech.ipynb](05_Speech_TextToSpeech.ipynb) | Tacotron-style text-to-mel network with location-sensitive attention, mel and stop-token losses | Small CMU ARCTIC speaker subset → speech with Griffin–Lim waveform reconstruction |
| Music | [06_Music_SymbolicGeneration.ipynb](06_Music_SymbolicGeneration.ipynb) | GPT over note/rest/duration events with next-event prediction | Bach chorales from music21 → monophonic melodies, piano rolls, and synthesized audio |
| 3D | [07_3D_PointCloudGeneration.ipynb](07_3D_PointCloudGeneration.ipynb) | Class-conditional PointNet-style VAE with Chamfer distance and KL regularization | Procedural sphere, cube, cone, cylinder, and torus → 512-point shapes |

**Start with the complete walkthrough:** [Multi-Modal_Generative_AI_Master_Notebook.ipynb](Multi-Modal_Generative_AI_Master_Notebook.ipynb).

## What you will learn

- Prepare text vocabularies, image transforms, video sequences, mel spectrograms, music events, and unordered point sets.
- Implement attention, autoregressive decoding, diffusion denoising, recurrent visual prediction, masked reconstruction, and variational sampling.
- Match each modality to a suitable loss and training strategy.
- Use checkpoints, loss plots, sample visualizations, and notebook audio playback to inspect behavior.
- Explore temperature/top-k sampling, diffusion guidance, image masking ratios, and conditional 3D generation.
- Compare a small model trained from scratch with optional pretrained inference paths.

## Setup and first run

Use an isolated Python environment supported by the PyTorch packages you install. A CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU is recommended for training. CPU execution is supported by the notebook device-selection logic but can take substantially longer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Multimodal-Generation-Lab.git
cd GenAI-Multimodal-Generation-Lab
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate the environment:

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate
```

Install a compatible `torch`, `torchvision`, and `torchaudio` set using the [official PyTorch installation selector](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/), choosing the build appropriate to your platform and GPU. Then install the remaining notebook dependencies:

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m jupyter lab
```

1. Open the master notebook for the full sequence, or select an individual modality notebook.
2. Select the kernel for your environment and run the global setup cells first.
3. Run the remaining cells in order. In the master notebook, later sections reuse earlier definitions, including GPT for symbolic music.
4. Allow dataset downloads on the first run. Keep the working directory at the repository root so relative paths resolve consistently.
5. Train the model before running its generation/demo cells. Adjust the step/epoch settings to your compute budget.

The setup cells also install `music21`, `soundfile`, and `imageio`. Optional pretrained paths may install additional packages and download model weights. Dependencies in `requirements.txt` are unpinned starting requirements, not a tested environment lockfile.

## Unified inference hub

After running the relevant training and definition cells in the master notebook, Section 8 constructs `hub` with seven modality routes:

```python
hub.generate("text", "ROMEO:", max_new_tokens=200)
hub.generate("image", "Sneaker", n_samples=4)
hub.generate("speech", "Hello from the multimodal notebook.")
hub.generate("3d", "sphere", n_samples=1)
```

The remaining routes are `video`, `vision`, and `music`; their inputs are context-frame tensors, image tensors, and music seed events respectively. Output types follow each notebook's generator. The hub is an in-memory dispatcher over initialized models, rather than an independently packaged service. The final section includes an illustrative Gradio UI example for text and image generation; a deployed application is not included.

## Project results gallery

The images below are extracted from existing notebook outputs. They illustrate a saved run and are not newly measured benchmarks.

### Video continuation

![Saved Moving-MNIST frame prediction output](assets/video-prediction.png)

ConvLSTM predictions illustrate how a recurrent visual model continues simple moving-digit sequences.

### Masked image reconstruction

![Original, masked, and reconstructed CIFAR-10 images](assets/masked-reconstruction.png)

The vision notebook compares an input image, its masked version, and the reconstructed image.

### Conditional 3D shapes

![Generated point clouds for five primitive shape classes](assets/point-clouds.png)

The 3D notebook samples class-conditioned point clouds from the VAE latent space.

## Optional pretrained paths

The notebooks include optional examples for GPT-2, Stable Diffusion, pretrained video diffusion, ViT-MAE, SpeechT5 with HiFi-GAN, MusicGen, and Shap-E. These paths are controlled by notebook flags and are off by default. Inspect each example before enabling it: model downloads, hardware requirements, dependencies, access conditions, and model licenses differ.

## Data, generated files, and repository layout

```text
.
├── README.md
├── requirements.txt
├── assets/                       # Result images used in this README
├── 01_Text_GPT.ipynb
├── 02_Image_Diffusion.ipynb
├── 03_Video_FramePrediction.ipynb
├── 04_Vision_MaskedImageModeling.ipynb
├── 05_Speech_TextToSpeech.ipynb
├── 06_Music_SymbolicGeneration.ipynb
├── 07_3D_PointCloudGeneration.ipynb
└── Multi-Modal_Generative_AI_Master_Notebook.ipynb
```

Datasets are downloaded or constructed by notebook cells. Runtime directories such as `data/`, `checkpoints/`, and `outputs/` are excluded from this public source snapshot. Existing inline notebook plots and audio are retained. Downloaded datasets and pretrained weights remain subject to their respective providers' terms.

## Compute, limitations, and reproducibility

The notebook narrative reports short training runs calibrated on an RTX 2060 with 6 GB VRAM. Treat those timings as author-reported examples, not guarantees: hardware, package versions, download time, and runtime configuration affect results. The publication work did not rerun training or independently verify those timings.

Expect limited long-range coherence in tiny text models, low-resolution diffusion samples, blur in video predictions, approximate masked-image reconstruction, and low-fidelity speech from short training and Griffin–Lim inversion. Music is monophonic with simple synthesized timbre. The 3D output is a point cloud with a fixed point count, not a textured mesh.

For repeatable experiments, record your package versions, random seed, device, dataset subset, training settings, and checkpoint. The notebooks provide seed and checkpoint helpers, but exact numerical agreement across devices is not guaranteed.

## Troubleshooting

- **GPU is not detected:** check `torch.cuda.is_available()` and install the appropriate PyTorch build for your platform and driver.
- **Missing variables or models:** restart the kernel and execute the notebook from its setup cells in order.
- **Out of GPU memory:** reduce batch size or model size and leave unused pretrained paths disabled.
- **Dataset download fails:** verify connectivity and write access to `data/`, then rerun the preparation cell.
- **Speech package/backend errors:** keep PyTorch-family versions compatible; the notebook uses `soundfile` for waveform reading to avoid relying on an optional torchaudio decoding backend.

## Extending the project

Possible next steps include larger datasets, longer training, polyphonic music encoding, neural speech vocoders, improved video generation objectives, point-cloud diffusion, and cross-modal conditioning. The master notebook discusses LoRA, quantization, and UI integration as extension ideas; these are not complete production features in this repository.

## Author and reuse

Maintained by [Vamshi Krishna Adam](https://github.com/vams2krish). Questions and reproducible bug reports can be shared through this repository's Issues tab. Include the notebook name, runtime versions, device, and relevant error message.

No project license has been selected in this publication. Public visibility alone does not grant an open-source license. Dataset, model, and dependency licenses apply separately.

# GenAI Startup Brief Agent

![GenAI Startup Brief Agent project overview](docs/project-overview.svg)

**Turn a startup idea into a structured business brief with LangChain and Ollama.**

A Python generative AI prototype with a browser interface and command-line entry points. Enter an idea, add context, select an Ollama model, and request a brief covering customers, competition, monetization, go-to-market strategy, risks, and financial assumptions.

**Project type:** Generative AI / LLM application  
**Stack:** Python · LangChain · Ollama · Node.js · Express · HTML/CSS/JavaScript

## Features

- Startup brief generation from a single idea and optional additional details.
- A prompt requesting 15 sections, including a Business Model Canvas and three-year financial projections with sensitivity analysis.
- Browser UI backed by an Express endpoint that launches the Python CLI.
- Dedicated startup CLI plus general single-prompt and interactive chat entry points.
- Model choices exposed by the CLIs: `llama3.2:latest`, `minimax-m2.5:cloud`, and `kimi-k2.5:cloud`. Availability depends on your Ollama instance and account.
- Deterministic stub output when the LangChain prompt or Ollama integration dependencies are missing.
- Model availability validation and configurable connection retries.

## Project visual

The image above is a project overview illustration, not a screenshot or a sample generated result.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[Startup idea and context] --> W[Browser UI]
    W --> E[Express: POST /api/startup-brief]
    E --> C[Python startup CLI]
    T[agent_startup.yaml] --> C
    C --> P[LangChain prompt]
    P --> O[ChatOllama]
    O --> M[Ollama model]
    M --> R[Generated brief]
    R --> W
```

`src/startup_prompt.py` loads the prompt from `agent_startup.yaml`, with a fallback if the file or marker is missing. `src/agent.py` composes a system/human prompt with `ChatOllama` at temperature zero. The UI server invokes `src/startup_agent_cli.py` and returns its stdout to the browser.

Despite the historical agent name, the current implementation is a prompt-to-model runnable; it does not implement autonomous tool calling, web research, retrieval, or a multi-agent workflow.

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10 or later.
- Node.js and npm for the browser UI.
- Ollama running with a model available under its exact tag.
- The existing UI launcher expects a Windows virtual environment at `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`.

### Install on Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Startup-Brief-Agent.git
cd GenAI-Startup-Brief-Agent
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r test_requirements.txt
npm --prefix ui ci
ollama pull llama3.2:latest
```

Ensure Ollama is running before generation. Run `ollama serve` in a separate terminal if it is not already running as an application/service.

### Configuration

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | `http://localhost:11434` | Ollama endpoint; used by validation and the Ollama client environment. |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL_LIST_RETRIES` | `5` | Connection attempts during model validation. |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL_LIST_RETRY_SLEEP_SECONDS` | `1` | Delay between validation attempts. |
| `SKIP_OLLAMA_MODEL_VALIDATION` | unset | Set to `1` to bypass the availability check; inference still requires Ollama. |
| `PORT` | `3000` | Express server port; set it in the shell that starts Node. |

The Python CLIs load `.env`. The Node server reads its process environment. An OpenAI API key is not used by the current implementation. Keep local configuration and secrets out of Git.

### Browser interface

Start from the **repository root** so the server resolves the Python executable and script correctly:

```powershell
node ui/server.js
```

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000), enter your startup idea and any extra context, choose a model, and submit the form.

### Startup brief CLI

```powershell
python src/startup_agent_cli.py --idea "A scheduling assistant for independent fitness coaches" --model llama3.2:latest
```

### General chat CLI

```powershell
python src/agent_cli.py --prompt "Explain product-market fit" --model llama3.2:latest
python src/agent_cli.py --interactive --model llama3.2:latest
```

Type `exit` or `quit` to end interactive mode. Exchanges are accumulated locally but are not included in subsequent model prompts.

## Brief contents

The prompt requests executive summary; startup idea; problem statement; target customers and personas; market sizing and trends; competition; differentiation; product and solution; nine-block Business Model Canvas; monetization; go-to-market strategy; metrics and milestones; three-year financial projections and sensitivity; risks and mitigations; and exit strategies.

These are model-generated drafts. There is no live source retrieval or numerical validation, so market claims, competitor details, and financial projections need independent verification.

## Repository layout

```text
.
├── README.md
├── .env.example
├── .gitignore
├── agent_startup.yaml       # Editable business brief prompt
├── requirements.txt        # Python runtime dependencies
├── test_requirements.txt   # Test dependencies
├── pyproject.toml          # Python project metadata
├── conftest.py
├── docs/project-overview.svg
├── src/
│   ├── agent.py            # Ollama validation and runnable factory
│   ├── agent_cli.py        # General chat CLI
│   ├── startup_agent_cli.py
│   ├── startup_prompt.py   # Prompt loading and rendering
│   ├── logging_config.py   # Optional logging configuration helper
│   └── tests/test_agent.py
└── ui/
    ├── index.html          # Browser interface
    ├── server.js           # Express and Python process bridge
    ├── package.json
    ├── package-lock.json
    └── README_UI.md
```

## Validation

```powershell
python -m pytest -q
node --check ui/server.js
```

The existing unit test checks that the agent can be constructed while model validation is patched out. It does not test live inference, response quality, or the browser-to-model flow.

## Current limitations and troubleshooting

- **Model missing / connection failure:** check `ollama list`, pull the exact model tag, and verify `OLLAMA_HOST`.
- **`[stub]` output:** required LangChain/Ollama dependencies were not imported; install the runtime requirements in the interpreter you are using.
- **UI launch directory:** use `node ui/server.js` from the root. Running `npm start` inside `ui` makes the current server resolve the wrong Python and script paths.
- **Platform support:** the Python code can run on other platforms, but the UI process launcher currently hardcodes the Windows virtual environment layout and has no implemented system-Python fallback.
- **Response handling:** the interactive chat path assumes a dictionary result even though the full runnable returns an AI message; it needs normalization for reliable interactive use. The startup CLI prints the raw message representation rather than extracting only its text.
- **Server hardening:** authentication, request timeouts, robust subprocess error handling, and deployment controls are not implemented. Use as a local development prototype.
- **Logging:** the CLIs use Loguru; file rotation is available in `configure_logging()` but the current entry points do not call that helper.
- Dependencies use lower bounds rather than a fully pinned Python lockfile.

## Customization

Edit `agent_startup.yaml` to change the requested brief sections. Keep the `startup_brainstorm_prompt: |` field and `{idea}` placeholder. Add model options consistently in the CLI argument choices and browser selector. Extend `build_agent()` to introduce additional prompt behavior or an actual tool-calling runtime.

No license has been selected for this repository. Add a license before distributing it under specific reuse terms.

projects.readme:
# GUI Desktop Browser

A Windows-oriented desktop web browser built with Python, PyQt6 and QtWebEngine, with tabbed browsing, automatic video discovery and integrated media downloads.

![Desktop Browser project overview](docs/images/desktop-browser.svg)

*Project overview illustration, not an application screenshot. The current window title and packaged executable retain the original “Private Browser” name.*

## Features

- Browse in multiple tabs with back, forward, reload and address-bar navigation.
- Enter a URL or search Google from the address bar.
- Discover video sources from page elements every three seconds, with a list of detected media.
- Download a selected video or paste a media/page URL into the download panel.
- Run downloads in background Qt threads and show progress and completion status.
- Try Streamlink first, then yt-dlp, then a direct HTTP download fallback.
- Optionally auto-download detected videos and move playing-video tabs toward the front (checked every five seconds).
- Clear detected videos and completed download entries.
- Access FFmpeg conversion, audio extraction and metadata helper methods in the source.

Support for an individual website, codec or stream depends on the installed dependencies and the site's behavior. DRM-protected media and blob URLs are not supported by the page scanner. FFmpeg helpers are source-level utilities, not a complete editing interface or an automatic conversion guarantee for every download.

## Requirements

- Windows is the intended packaging and installation target. Other operating systems have not been validated for this repository.
- Python 3.10 or newer is required by the source's type-annotation syntax; use a version supported by the current PyQt6 wheels.
- Dependencies listed in `requirements.txt`: PyQt6, PyQt6-WebEngine, requests, yt-dlp, streamlink and ffmpeg-python.
- FFmpeg and FFprobe executables on `PATH` for media-processing helpers. The `ffmpeg-python` package alone does not install these executables.
- An internet connection for remote browsing and downloads.

## Run from source

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GUI-Desktop-Browser.git
cd GUI-Desktop-Browser
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe main.py
```

The app starts on Google. No administrator permissions are required for running the source application.

## Usage

1. Enter a website address or search phrase and press Enter or click **Go**.
2. Use **+** to open another tab and the tab close control to close one.
3. Wait for the **Detected Videos** list to populate on a page containing supported video sources.
4. Select an entry and click **Download Selected Video**, or paste a URL into the right-hand input and click **Download**.
5. Monitor **Active Downloads**. Files are written to `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\BrowserDownloads`.
6. Enable **Auto-download detected videos** only when you want detected media to download automatically.

For streams whose total size is unknown, progress may be approximate. A download can fail even when a media URL is detected, particularly when authentication, expiring URLs or site-specific playback logic is involved. Download only media you have permission to save.

## Architecture

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | Main window, navigation, tabs, download panel, background download workers and tab reordering |
| `browser_tab.py` | QtWebEngine view, JavaScript video discovery and media-processing helpers |
| `utils.py` | Logging, filename cleanup and opening folders |
| `requirements.txt` | Python runtime dependencies |
| `simple-browser.spec` | Existing PyInstaller packaging recipe |
| `version_info.txt` | Windows executable version metadata |
| `install.bat` | Installs an already-built executable and creates shortcuts |
| `docs/images/desktop-browser.svg` | Illustrated project overview |

The main download worker attempts Streamlink, then yt-dlp, and finally a streamed requests download. Browser discovery and download extraction are separate steps; the downloader does not automatically receive the browser's authenticated session.

## Windows packaging

Install PyInstaller separately:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install pyinstaller
```

The existing spec expects these externally supplied binaries:

```text
ffmpeg-master-latest-win64-gpl/bin/ffmpeg.exe
ffmpeg-master-latest-win64-gpl/bin/ffplay.exe
ffmpeg-master-latest-win64-gpl/bin/ffprobe.exe
```

After supplying them, the intended build command is:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m PyInstaller simple-browser.spec
```

The spec also references `os.path.exists` without explicitly importing `os`; review that import when preparing a build. The recipe targets `dist/PrivateBrowser.exe`. It is retained from the original project and may require adjustments for the installed PyInstaller version; a fresh executable build has not been verified for this publication. `install.bat` copies that executable into Program Files and creates desktop and Start Menu shortcuts, so that installation step needs administrator privileges. It does not install Python dependencies or build the app.

No prebuilt executable, FFmpeg distribution or release download is included in this initial repository.

## Local data and privacy

- Downloads are saved in the user's Downloads folder.
- `utils.py` writes diagnostics to `browser.log` in the working directory.
- QtWebEngine enables JavaScript and local storage and uses a browser profile. The project does not explicitly enforce an off-the-record profile or guarantee that history and cookies are erased.
- The source enables autoplay and mixed content and changes the user-agent string. The current “Private Browser” window title should not be interpreted as a verified privacy or security guarantee.
- There is no documented settings-file interface; configure behavior through the existing UI or source.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Missing PyQt6 or WebEngine imports | Install requirements with the same virtual-environment Python used to launch the app |
| FFmpeg/FFprobe not found | Install the executables and confirm `ffmpeg -version` and `ffprobe -version` work |
| Videos are not detected | Allow a few seconds after playback starts; some pages expose only blob URLs or protected players |
| Site downloads fail | Update yt-dlp and Streamlink in the virtual environment and retry with the original page URL |
| Packaging fails | Verify the FFmpeg paths in the spec and its compatibility with your PyInstaller version |
| Unexpected behavior | Review the local `browser.log`; remove personal URLs before sharing diagnostics |

## Development and verification

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m compileall main.py browser_tab.py utils.py
```

For manual checks, launch the app, navigate to a page, open and close tabs, test discovery with media you control, and verify a small permitted download reaches the output directory. Python compilation passed for this publication. Application launch attempts exited before a screenshot could be captured in the publishing environment, including Python 3.11 and 3.14 attempts. Runtime behavior, external website downloads and the installer remain unverified. The image above is an overview illustration.

Report reproducible bugs and feature requests in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/vams2krish/GUI-Desktop-Browser/issues). Include the Python/Windows versions, dependency versions, reproduction steps and a sanitized error message.

## Project status and licensing

This repository publishes a clean source snapshot of the existing Simple-Browser project under the GUI-Desktop-Browser repository name. Generated binaries, build output, logs, bytecode and downloaded third-party archives are excluded.

No project license file has been supplied. Do not assume an MIT or other open-source license from this repository's public visibility. Dependencies and any separately acquired FFmpeg binaries retain their respective licenses.

projects.readme:
# ImmigrationBot

### Waypoint — a private U.S. immigration workspace

**Organize your next chapter with local AI, a personalized document plan, and a clear application timeline.**

ImmigrationBot is the repository for **Waypoint**, a browser-based immigration preparation assistant powered by locally installed Ollama models. Chat and document retrieval run on your own machine, without uploading your documents to ChatGPT or Claude.

![Waypoint dashboard — local AI, document progress, and case tracking](docs/images/waypoint-dashboard.png)

> **Project status:** Working single-user local application. Local chat, document embeddings, checklist progress, PDF export, and timelines are implemented. Case-status and processing-time lookups require a configured provider adapter and credentials. Automatic1111 detection is optional; it is not the chat engine.

## At a glance

| Capability | What is included |
| --- | --- |
| Private assistant | Local Ollama chat, selectable downloaded models, conversation context, and explicit error states |
| Optional RAG | Import PDF, TXT, or Markdown; local chunking and embeddings; vector retrieval; document/chunk references |
| Case tracker | Receipt validation, provider-backed status requests, saved results, refresh by receipt, and removal |
| Processing times | Form and office filters, provider estimate and source, with no fabricated estimates |
| Personalized checklist | Visa/application path, location, dependents, translation needs, and saved completion status |
| PDF export | Download the current checklist, completed items, timeline, notice dates, and official references |
| Visual timeline | Suggested preparation dates plus separately entered dates from official notices |
| Local integrations | Ollama health/model discovery and optional Automatic1111 API/model detection |
| Interface | Responsive dashboard, keyboard-accessible controls, dialog focus management, and connection settings |

[Quick start](#run) · [Privacy](#local-ai-and-privacy) · [API setup](#case-status-and-processing-time-api-adapter) · [Application paths](#checklists-and-timeline) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

[Download an example checklist PDF](docs/examples/sample-document-checklist.pdf) — generated from a generic H-1B preparation profile, with no applicant data or real case information.


A local React + Express application for private Ollama chat, optional retrieval augmented generation (RAG), personalized preparation checklists, PDF downloads, receipt tracking, and visual timelines.

## Run

Requires Node.js 20.19+ (or 22.12+), npm, Git, and a running local [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) installation. Node.js 22 LTS or newer is a convenient choice.

The default models are `llama3.2:latest` for chat and `nomic-embed-text-v2-moe:latest` for embeddings. Install these through Ollama if they are not already downloaded, or select compatible installed models in Settings. Model weights are not bundled in this repository.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/ImmigrationBot.git
cd ImmigrationBot
npm ci
Copy-Item .env.example .env
npm run dev
```

On macOS/Linux, use `cp .env.example .env` instead of `Copy-Item`.

Open http://127.0.0.1:4317. The server binds to loopback only. No hosting or public deployment is required.

```powershell
npm run build
$env:NODE_ENV = 'production'
npm start
```

`npm test` runs domain and isolated server integration checks. Tests use synthetic providers/models and a temporary data directory; they do not modify the personal workspace. `node tests/live-smoke.mjs` optionally tests real local inference and embeddings, using a clearly marked synthetic document that is removed afterward.

## Local AI and privacy

- Chat defaults to the downloaded `llama3.2:latest` model; retrieval uses `nomic-embed-text-v2-moe:latest`. Change these in Settings.
- Both models must already be downloaded. The app never pulls models or uses a cloud fallback. Remote-backed aliases, even those named `:latest`, are excluded.
- `OLLAMA_URL` must be a loopback host. The default uses `localhost`, which also reaches Ollama's IPv6 listener on Windows.
- Uploaded PDF/TXT/Markdown files are parsed in memory, chunked, and embedded by local Ollama. Text and vectors are stored in `data/workspace.json`; original upload binaries are not retained. Scanned PDFs need OCR before import.
- RAG can be toggled off in Assistant. RAG answers show retrieved document/chunk references; the model is instructed to acknowledge insufficient evidence. Generated responses still require verification.
- Chats are held in browser memory for the current session. Case receipts are sent only to the configured case provider when tracking is requested. Files and chat text are never sent to the case provider.
- `data/` and `.env` are ignored by Git. Protect the local disk and backups: stored data is not encrypted by this app.
- This is a **single-user local implementation**, not an authenticated multi-customer production service. Add authentication, per-user data isolation, encryption, access controls and deployment review before operating for multiple customers.

## Automatic1111

Settings detects the local Automatic1111 API and installed image models at `AUTOMATIC1111_URL` (default port 7860). It was not running during setup. If you want detection, start your existing installation with its API enabled (`--api`). Automatic1111 is an image engine; immigration chat and retrieval use Ollama. No image generation is needed for the requested workflow.

## Case status and processing-time API adapter

No provider key was supplied. The app does **not** invent live results. It displays a clear connection message until configured. Configure a third-party provider or a server-side adapter for your provider's contract in `.env`, then restart:

```dotenv
CASE_API_URL=https://your-provider.example/cases/{receipt}
PROCESSING_API_URL=https://your-provider.example/processing-times
CASE_API_KEY=your-provider-token
```

These are examples of the adapter contract, not a claimed real vendor endpoint. Both requests use `Authorization: Bearer <CASE_API_KEY>` when configured. Secrets stay on the server. For a vendor using different authentication or response fields, adapt the `provider()` function and normalization in `server.js` to its documented API.

`GET CASE_API_URL` substitutes the normalized receipt into `{receipt}`. Expected JSON:

```json
{
  "form": "I-129",
  "status": "Case Was Received",
  "description": "Provider-supplied status details",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-27"
}
```

`form` and `status` are required strings. No live sample is preloaded. Receipt validation requires three letters and ten digits. Saved cases can be refreshed by entering the same receipt again, or removed from the dashboard.

`GET PROCESSING_API_URL` adds `visa`, `form`, and `office` query parameters. Expected JSON:

```json
{
  "estimate": "Provider-supplied current estimate",
  "asOf": "2026-10-27",
  "office": "Requested service center",
  "sourceUrl": "https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times/"
}
```

Processing-time lookup is available on the Overview dashboard and in Settings, and is specific to the requested form/office. Estimates do not predict a particular case completion date. Until a provider is configured, the UI links to official USCIS processing times. USCIS's own Case Status API is a separate integration requiring approved access; no USCIS credentials or access are implied here: https://developer.uscis.gov/api/case-status.

## Checklists and timeline

Supported preparation paths:

- H-1B petition preparation, with consular documents added for applicants outside the U.S.
- F-1 consular visa preparation (not an I-539 change-of-status checklist).
- Family-based adjustment of status inside the U.S. (not family consular processing).

Dependents and translation needs add conditional documents. These are general preparation lists, not exhaustive eligibility determinations; category-specific requirements, exemptions and filing windows must be confirmed against current official instructions. Checklists do not calculate fees or determine eligibility.

A user-selected target date generates preparation milestones at -35, -14 and 0 days, and item-specific suggested preparation dates. These are explicitly labeled **planning targets**, not government deadlines. Official notice dates can be entered separately. No USCIS deadline is inferred automatically.

Download PDF uses the same current checklist, completed items, profile, planning milestones and notice dates. It includes clickable official sources. No cloud PDF service is used.

Official reference sources:

- H-1B checklist: https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/m-735.pdf
- Student visa instructions: https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/student-visa.html
- I-485 instructions: https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/i-485instr.pdf

## Files and configuration

- `server.js`: local HTTP server, integrations, RAG and PDF export
- `domain.js`: document rules, date arithmetic and retrieval helpers
- `src/main.jsx`, `src/style.css`: responsive workspace UI
- `tests/`: domain and server integration tests
- `.env.example`: configuration template
- `data/workspace.json`: private local persistence (created on first save)

If port 4317 is occupied, set `PORT` in `.env`. Keep the server on loopback. Large Ollama models may load slowly on memory-constrained machines; select a smaller downloaded model in Settings.


## Architecture

The application uses a React 19 interface, Vite 7, an Express 5 local server, Ollama's HTTP API, PDFKit for PDF generation, Multer for bounded in-memory uploads, and pdf-parse for text extraction.

```text
Browser on this device
  |
  +-- React dashboard, assistant, checklist, timeline, knowledge base
  |
  +-- Express API (127.0.0.1 only)
        |
        +-- Local Ollama: chat + embedding generation
        +-- Local JSON workspace: profile, vectors, document text, progress, notices, cases
        +-- PDFKit: downloadable checklist PDF
        +-- Optional case/processing provider: receipt and lookup filters only
        +-- Optional Automatic1111: health and model discovery
```

### How local RAG works

1. Import a supported text-based document through Knowledge base.
2. The server extracts text and splits it into overlapping chunks.
3. The selected local embedding model embeds each chunk.
4. Text and vectors are saved in the local workspace file.
5. With Knowledge base enabled, the assistant embeds your question and ranks compatible document chunks by cosine similarity.
6. The highest-ranking chunks are supplied to the selected local chat model as evidence.
7. The answer includes document/chunk reference metadata for inspection.

Changing the embedding model requires reimporting documents so their vectors use the same model. Retrieval references are not a guarantee of factual or legal correctness; review the actual source and current official instructions.

### Configuration reference

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and restart after changing server configuration.

| Variable | Default / purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `4317`; local application port |
| `OLLAMA_URL` | `http://localhost:11434`; must be a loopback host |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL` | `llama3.2:latest`; initial chat model for a new workspace |
| `OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL` | `nomic-embed-text-v2-moe:latest`; initial embedding model |
| `AUTOMATIC1111_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:7860`; optional image-engine discovery |
| `CASE_API_URL` | Optional adapter URL containing `{receipt}` |
| `PROCESSING_API_URL` | Optional adapter URL accepting form, office, and visa query parameters |
| `CASE_API_KEY` | Optional server-side bearer token used by the provider adapter |
| `APP_TIMEZONE` | `America/Los_Angeles`; date used in PDF exports |
| `DATA_DIR` | Optional private workspace directory; defaults to `data/` |
| `NODE_ENV` | Set to `production` to serve the built `dist/` application |

After a workspace is created, its model choices are saved in the workspace. Change those in Settings; environment defaults do not overwrite saved selections.

### Local HTTP endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/workspace` | Profile, checklist, milestones, saved cases, document metadata |
| GET | `/api/health` | Local AI, installed models, optional image engine, provider configuration |
| PUT | `/api/profile` | Save preparation path and personal planning options |
| PUT | `/api/completed` | Save completed checklist item IDs |
| PUT | `/api/settings` | Select downloaded local chat and embedding models |
| POST | `/api/documents` | Import one PDF/TXT/Markdown file as multipart field `file` |
| DELETE | `/api/documents/:id` | Remove an imported document and its stored chunks/vectors |
| POST | `/api/chat` | Ask a question with optional retrieval and recent conversation context |
| POST | `/api/cases` | Look up and save a provider-backed receipt status |
| DELETE | `/api/cases/:receipt` | Remove a saved case |
| GET | `/api/processing` | Request a provider estimate with `form` and `office` filters |
| POST | `/api/notices` | Add a user-entered notice title and date |
| DELETE | `/api/notices/:id` | Remove a notice date |
| GET | `/api/checklist.pdf` | Download the current preparation checklist |

These endpoints are designed for this single local workspace. They are not a public authenticated service API.

## Validation

```powershell
npm test
npm run build
```

The automated suite covers receipt validation, conditional document rules, calendar-date arithmetic and invalid dates, retrieval scoring/chunking, local-model filtering (including cloud-backed aliases), provider adapters, document import/retrieval/deletion, citations, persistence, PDF signatures, and cross-origin mutation rejection.

The application was also checked in a browser, exported PDF pages were rendered and visually inspected, and real local Ollama chat and embedding requests were exercised. Provider integration tests use synthetic responses; no live third-party case-status service is represented as configured. Model startup latency depends on hardware and available memory.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Ollama offline | Start Ollama and check `OLLAMA_URL`; the Windows listener may require `localhost` rather than `127.0.0.1` |
| Model not available | Select a downloaded local model in Settings; cloud models and remote aliases are rejected |
| Chat takes too long | Allow for a cold model load, free memory, or select a smaller installed chat model |
| Model returns no final answer | Choose a compatible non-thinking chat model or retry a shorter question |
| Document import fails | Use PDF/TXT/Markdown under 10 MB with readable text; OCR scanned pages before import |
| RAG stops after a model change | Reimport documents with the current embedding model |
| Case tracker says not configured | Set the provider URLs/token, implement any vendor-specific mapping, and restart |
| Address already in use | Choose another free `PORT` in `.env` |
| Automatic1111 not running | Start the existing installation with API access enabled; chat does not require it |
| Workspace data unreadable | Restore the private workspace file from a trusted backup; corrupted data is not silently reset |

## Scope and next steps

Implemented functionality is described above. Multi-user accounts, authentication, encrypted storage, a managed vector database, automatic official-source refresh, notifications, automatic government-deadline calculation, OCR, additional immigration categories, and a specific vendor's production case-status integration are **not implemented**.

Before serving multiple customers, add authenticated tenant isolation, secure storage and backups, access controls, retention controls, and a reviewed deployment architecture. Do not expose this unauthenticated l
