projects.readme:
# StoryTime

**Little stories. Big dreams.** A cozy AI storytelling app for children and the grown-ups who read with them, powered by local models.

StoryTime turns a child's favorite character into personalized bedtime stories, interactive adventures, printable books, and narrated reading sessions. It uses **Ollama** for story text, **Automatic1111** for cover illustrations, and an optional **local Kokoro-compatible speech service** for AI narration.

![StoryTime app preview](docs/images/storytime-preview.png)

## Features

| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **My Little Heroes** | Save and edit a character's name, favorite color, and favorite animal. Include those preferences in future stories. |
| **Personalized stories** | Select a hero, theme, and optional idea to generate an original bedtime story with Ollama. |
| **Choose your own adventure** | Three chapters with two decision points, offering 2–3 choices each. Previous chapters and the selected choice shape the next chapter and ending. |
| **Illustrated covers** | Generate watercolor-style covers with the currently loaded Automatic1111 checkpoint. Retry failed illustrations without losing the story. |
| **Our bookshelf** | Reopen saved stories and continue unfinished adventures. |
| **Download as PDF** | Export an A5 book with cover artwork, paginated text, chapter headings, page numbers, and the selected adventure path. |
| **Listen to Story** | Hear gentle-paced narration with an installed device voice or optional local AI speech service. |
| **Reading Rewards** | Unlock stickers after 1, 5, and 10 different stories, and after exploring 3 themes. Each book earns completion credit once. |
| **Local AI settings** | Discover installed completion models and configure localhost service endpoints and voices. Cloud models are excluded from discovery. |

Themes include **Enchanted forest**, **Space explorers**, **Ocean wonders**, and **Magical kingdoms**.

## Technology

- **Frontend:** HTML, responsive CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
- **Backend:** Node.js and Express, serving the app and proxying local AI requests.
- **Stories:** Ollama `/api/chat` with JSON output.
- **Illustrations:** Automatic1111 `/sdapi/v1/txt2img`.
- **Narration:** Browser Speech Synthesis or local `/v1/audio/speech`.
- **PDFs:** jsPDF, generated in the browser.
- **Storage:** Browser `localStorage`; no database or account required.
- **Tests:** Node.js test runner with mock local AI services.

## Quick start

Install Node.js 22 or newer and npm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/StoryTime.git
cd StoryTime
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:4173**. Both `npm run dev` and `npm start` run the Express server. Restart it after server-side changes and refresh the browser after frontend changes.

To use another port in PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:PORT = "4180"
npm run dev
```

### Configure Ollama

Install [Ollama](https://ollama.com), start its local service, and download a story model:

```sh
ollama pull llama3.2
```

If Ollama is not already running through its desktop app, run `ollama serve`. The default model is `llama3.2:latest`. In **Local AI settings**, click **Find local models**, select a model, and save.

### Configure Automatic1111

Install [Stable Diffusion WebUI](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui), load a checkpoint, and start it with `--api`.

For a standard Windows installation, add the flag to `webui-user.bat`:

```bat
set COMMANDLINE_ARGS=--api
```

Keep any existing flags and append `--api` if needed. The default address is `http://localhost:7860`. The app uses the currently loaded checkpoint and requests 512 × 640 cover images. Cover generation can be unchecked when creating a story.

### Configure narration

Device narration needs no separate speech server when the browser supports Speech Synthesis and has an installed voice. Choose a voice in the reader's **Reading voice** selector.

For AI narration, run a local Kokoro-compatible server accepting `POST /v1/audio/speech`. Enter its origin and voice ID in **Local AI settings**.

| Setting | Default / example |
| --- | --- |
| Ollama address | `http://localhost:11434` |
| Story model | `llama3.2:latest` |
| Automatic1111 address | `http://localhost:7860` |
| AI speech address | Empty by default; example: `http://localhost:8880` |
| AI speech model sent to service | `kokoro` |
| AI speech voice | `af_heart` |
| AI narration speed | `0.85` |

Ollama and Automatic1111 do not synthesize speech. A grandparent-like voice depends on the speech model or device voice installed; this repository does not ship a dedicated grandparent voice model.

## Your first adventure

1. Create a character in **My Little Heroes** with a name, favorite color, and favorite animal.
2. Select **Tell my story**, choose a theme, and optionally add an idea.
3. Enable **Choose your own adventure** for an interactive story, or leave it off for a complete bedtime tale.
4. Generate the story. If enabled, cover illustration runs after the text is saved.
5. Read together, listen, or download a PDF.
6. Follow adventure choices to the ending and select **We finished this story!** to earn reading credit.
7. Visit **Reading Rewards** to see unlocked stickers and progress.

## Project structure

```text
StoryTime/
├── public/
│   ├── index.html          # App shell
│   ├── app.js              # Heroes, stories, reader, rewards, narration, PDF
│   └── style.css           # Responsive design and decorative illustrations
├── server.mjs              # Express server and local AI proxies
├── tests/api.test.mjs      # API tests with mock services
├── docs/images/            # Project screenshots
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

## API overview

All app endpoints accept JSON via `POST`. Configured service origins must use `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or IPv6 loopback.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/models` | Discover local Ollama completion models. |
| `/api/story` | Generate a complete story or adventure chapter from hero, theme, history, and choice. |
| `/api/cover` | Request an illustration and return a PNG data URL. |
| `/api/speech` | Send text to a configured local speech service and return MP3 audio. |

## Tests and verification

```sh
npm test
```

Four automated API tests cover model filtering, hero preferences and adventure history, final chapter choices, localhost restrictions, and cover response formatting. These tests use mock services and need no downloaded models.

The initial implementation passed all four API tests, JavaScript syntax checks, and a browser check of profile creation. Live Ollama inference timed out while its model runner loaded. Automatic1111 was offline during initial verification. Full live story, image, speech, and PDF workflows still need end-to-end validation against running services; the automated tests do not certify those workflows.

## Storage, privacy, and current limitations

- Heroes, stories, covers, settings, and rewards are saved in this browser on this device. Clearing site data removes them. There is no account system or cross-device synchronization.
- Download PDFs to preserve books outside the browser. Large cover collections may fill browser storage.
- The server binds to `127.0.0.1`. This is a local development app without internet hosting, authentication, or multi-user configuration.
- AI requests go to configured loopback services. CSS also requests Google Fonts, with system-font fallbacks when unavailable.
- Prompts request gentle stories for ages 4–8, but model output is not guaranteed. Grown-ups should preview stories.
- Adventures are generated chapter by chapter; the saved book retains the chosen path rather than every possible branch.
- Unfinished adventure PDFs include only generated chapters and a continuation note.
- PDF export uses built-in fonts with limited Unicode coverage; Latin-script names and stories work best.
- Speed depends on model size, RAM/VRAM, and other workloads. Cold model loading can take several minutes.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No models found | Start Ollama, verify its address, and refresh models in Settings. |
| Generation times out | Try a smaller installed completion model, check Ollama logs, and allow it to finish loading. |
| Incomplete story response | Retry or use a model that follows JSON instructions reliably. |
| Cover unavailable | Start Automatic1111 with `--api` and a checkpoint loaded. Use **Illustrate this cover** to retry. |
| No narration | Check installed device voices or the configured speech endpoint and voice ID. |
| Port already in use | Choose another `PORT` and open its matching loopback address. |
| Saved data missing | Use the same browser and origin. Clearing site data or private browsing affects storage. |

## References

- [Ollama API](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md)
- [Automatic1111 API](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui/wiki/API)
- [jsPDF](https://github.com/parallax/jsPDF)

Built for little dreamers and the grown-ups who love them.

# VentureLink

### Opportunity, aligned.

A membership platform connecting ambitious businesses with aligned investors. VentureLink combines profile discovery, compatibility matching, private conversations, pitch decks, document verification, and manual administration in a cohesive, responsive experience.

![VentureLink homepage](docs/images/venturelink-preview.jpg)

**[Visit the deployed site](https://venturelink.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site)** · [Features](#features) · [Getting started](#getting-started) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Launch checklist](#launch-checklist)

> **Status:** The application is deployed privately. Live payment collection requires Stripe configuration and a reachable webhook endpoint. A public GitHub repository does not change the website's private access policy.

## Overview

Finding capital or an investment opportunity is about more than a funding number. VentureLink helps both parties explain their goals, discover relevant profiles, and start a conversation around a shared vision.

- **Businesses** describe their vision, sector, funding requirements, location, stage, and partnership needs.
- **Investors** share investment preferences, budget, location, stage, and the businesses they want to support.
- **Administrators** review registrations and documents, approve or deactivate profiles, and monitor collected subscription revenue.

The interface uses warm neutrals, restrained green accents, generous spacing, consistent cards and forms, and responsive layouts for desktop and mobile.

## Features

| Area | Included behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Registration | Role-specific investor and business onboarding, sector, country, funding budget, stage, and open-ended goals |
| Authentication | Platform-owned ChatGPT sign-in and sign-out with user-specific account records |
| Membership | Stripe Checkout integration for a recurring $10 monthly **or** $10 yearly membership |
| Billing | Stripe Customer Portal integration for billing management and cancellation once configured |
| Discovery | Search by name or description; filter by role, sector, funding amount, country, and verified status |
| Matching | Rank opposite-party profiles and suggest up to five compatible matches |
| Connections | Send a private introduction; acceptance opens further messaging |
| Inbox | Requests, active conversations, persisted message history, and direct replies |
| Live updates | Authenticated Server-Sent Events with periodic change detection and a refresh fallback |
| Pitch decks | Upload PDFs or images and display authorized file links on profile cards and dialogs |
| Verification | Private identity or business-registration documents; manual review controls Verified badges |
| Administration | Registration list, approval, deactivation, verification, and collected-revenue totals |
| Profile reminders | Dashboard prompts to review profile details at the selected monthly or yearly interval |
| Responsive design | Shared navigation, mobile layouts, keyboard-accessible controls, and profile dialogs |

## Membership and access

The current pricing is **$10 per month or $10 per year**, according to the member's preference. There is no additional one-time registration charge.

1. Sign in and prepare an investor or business profile.
2. Save the profile and complete Stripe Checkout when payments are configured.
3. Upload a pitch deck, verification documents, or both as appropriate.
4. An administrator reviews the profile and any verification documents.
5. Approved, paid members can discover real profiles, request connections, and message accepted connections.

Payment, profile approval, and document verification are separate states. Uploading a document does not automatically verify a member. Editing a profile sends it for re-approval and clears its verification badge.

## Matching model

Matches are recomputed from current profile preferences and ranked using:

| Factor | Weight |
| --- | ---: |
| Sector alignment | 40% |
| Investment stage | 20% |
| Country | 15% |
| Proportional funding alignment | 25% |

Only approved, paid profiles from the opposite party are suggested. The dashboard displays at most five matches; fewer appear when the eligible network is smaller. Compatibility scores are heuristics, not investment recommendations or guarantees of funding.

## Messaging and privacy

- Contact email addresses are not published in Discovery or automatically shared in conversations.
- Requests include an introduction; further replies require acceptance.
- Conversation actions check participation and both members' active status.
- Messages and connection records persist in D1.
- Authenticated event streams check for changes every two seconds, reconnect after approximately 50 seconds, and use a 15-second refresh fallback.
- Members choose whether to share personal contact details in a message.

## Uploads and verification

Supported formats are **PDF, JPG, and PNG**, limited to **10 MB per upload**. The server checks MIME types and file signatures before storing files in R2.

- **Pitch decks:** Accessible to their owner, administrators, and approved, paid members when the publishing profile remains active.
- **Verification documents:** Accessible only to their owner and authorized administrators.
- **Verified badge:** Applied manually after a document exists for review. It does not endorse a business or guarantee an investment outcome.

## Pages

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Marketing homepage, illustrative profiles, and membership information |
| `/register` | Investor and business onboarding |
| `/dashboard` | Membership status, connection counts, top matches, and review reminders |
| `/discovery` | Search and filter the network |
| `/inbox` | Connection requests and active conversations |
| `/settings` | Profile details, billing, pitch decks, and verification documents |
| `/admin` | Administrator-only review and revenue monitoring |
| `/privacy` | Privacy, membership, and trust information |

Unknown routes return a 404. Before membership approval, profiles are clearly identified as illustrative and cannot receive real connection requests.

## Technology stack

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Interface | React 19, TypeScript, CSS, Lucide icons |
| Framework | Vinext with Next.js-compatible routing |
| Build | Vite and the Cloudflare Vite integration |
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers |
| Data | Cloudflare D1 / SQLite, Drizzle ORM and migrations |
| Files | Cloudflare R2 |
| Identity | Sites-managed ChatGPT authentication |
| Payments | Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal, and signed webhooks |
| Live conversations | Server-Sent Events |
| Hosting | Sites |

## Architecture

The React interface calls server routes that validate identity, permissions, and membership before reading or changing data.

```text
Browser / React UI
        |
        +-- /api/platform ------ identity + access checks
        |                              |
        |                              +-- D1: profiles, connections, messages,
        |                              |       uploads, payments, billing
        |                              +-- R2: pitch decks + private documents
        |                              +-- Stripe: checkout + billing portal
        |
        +-- /api/events -------- authenticated conversation-change stream
        |
Stripe -- /api/stripe/webhook -- signature checks + billing reconciliation
```

### Source layout

```text
app/
  platform.tsx                  Shared application views and interactions
  globals.css                   Responsive visual system
  chatgpt-auth.ts                Sign-in and identity helpers
  [section]/page.tsx            Dashboard, Discovery, Inbox, and account pages
  api/platform/route.ts         Profiles, uploads, payments, messaging, admin API
  api/events/route.ts           Authenticated live-update stream
  api/stripe/webhook/route.ts   Signed Stripe webhook processing
components/                     Shared starter UI components
db/                             D1 connection and schema declarations
drizzle/                        SQL migrations and schema metadata
docs/images/                    README project screenshot
scripts/                        Runtime, build, and local-preview tooling
tests/integration.py            Local onboarding and access-control checks
worker/index.ts                 Production Worker entry point
.openai/hosting.json             Sites identity and D1/R2 declarations
```

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Node.js **22.13.0 or newer**
- npm and Git
- Python 3 for the included local integration checks

### Install and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/VentureLink.git
cd VentureLink
npm ci
npm run dev
```

The portable development preview normally serves at **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. Use the address printed by the server if a different port is selected.

Local sign-in uses a development-only identity (`seedy@sites.test`). The mock authentication shim is excluded from production builds. Hosted authentication depends on Sites; this repository is not a standalone password-authentication service.

### Initialize local storage

The hosting manifest declares the `DB` D1 binding and `BUCKET` R2 binding. Build once to generate the local Worker configuration:

```bash
npm run build
```

Apply each migration once, in order:

```bash
node --import ./scripts/sites-env.mjs ./node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js d1 execute DB --local --config dist/server/wrangler.json --persist-to .wrangler/state --file drizzle/0000_flat_lady_mastermind.sql
node --import ./scripts/sites-env.mjs ./node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js d1 execute DB --local --config dist/server/wrangler.json --persist-to .wrangler/state --file drizzle/0001_equal_warbound.sql
```

Local and production databases are separate. Do not replay applied migrations. After schema changes, run `npm run db:generate`, inspect the generated SQL, and apply only new migrations.

### Runtime configuration

The `.env.example` file lists required configuration names. Configure actual values as hosted runtime secrets or appropriate ignored local runtime configuration.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Server-side Stripe API access |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Incoming webhook signature validation |
| `ADMIN_EMAILS` | Comma-separated administrator email allowlist |

Never put actual secrets into source files, the hosting manifest, or browser code. Local environment files, runtime state, databases, and build output are ignored by Git.

## Stripe setup

1. Configure the Stripe secret key and webhook signing secret for the runtime.
2. Enable and configure the Customer Portal, including cancellation.
3. Register a publicly reachable snapshot-event endpoint at `/api/stripe/webhook`.
4. Subscribe to:

```text
checkout.session.completed
invoice.paid
invoice.payment_failed
customer.subscription.updated
customer.subscription.deleted
customer.subscription.paused
customer.subscription.resumed
```

5. Test Checkout, renewal, cancellation, failed payments, and portal access in Stripe test mode before activating live payments.

Checkout returns are verified server-side. Webhooks use HMAC signature validation and timestamp tolerance. Invoice identifiers deduplicate recorded payments so an initial checkout and its invoice do not count as two payments. Subscription status controls paid access; admin approval remains independent.

Admin revenue reports recorded collected payments in USD before Stripe fees. It is not a net-revenue report, refund ledger, or monthly recurring revenue calculation.

References: [Stripe webhooks](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks) and [subscription events](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/webhooks).

## Validation

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run build
```

With the development server running and local migrations applied:

```bash
python tests/integration.py
```

The integration script creates a synthetic local profile and verification document. Use only a disposable local development database.

The initial implementation was reviewed on desktop and mobile. **43 local checks** passed across onboarding and uploads, connections, accepted replies and event streams, administration and privacy, webhook signatures, and production page responses. Some checks used temporary local harnesses rather than the committed integration script. Live Stripe transactions have not been exercised because account credentials are still required.

## Deployment

The checkout retains the original Sites identity in `.openai/hosting.json`. Publishing to that project requires the owner's Sites access. For an independent deployment, create a separate Sites project and use its returned identity instead of reusing the original ID.

Production publication packages the Worker and assets, synchronizes the exact source state, applies migrations, and deploys a saved version through Sites. Configure secrets through the hosting platform. Never commit deployment credentials.

The existing deployment is **owner-private**. Publishing this repository does not make the website public, expose its database, or give repository visitors administrator access.

## Launch checklist

- [ ] Connect the intended Stripe account and configure runtime secrets.
- [ ] Configure the Customer Portal and webhook endpoint.
- [ ] Complete end-to-end Stripe test-mode and renewal/cancellation testing.
- [ ] Confirm the $10 monthly / $10 yearly pricing.
- [ ] Explicitly configure the website's audience for customer enrollment.
- [ ] Add the operator's business identity, support contact, and terms.
- [ ] Define verification procedures, document retention, and deletion handling.
- [ ] Review abuse prevention, monitoring, backup, and recovery for expected traffic.

## Current boundaries

- Profile-review reminders appear inside the dashboard; reminder emails are not implemented.
- Bookmarks last for the current page session.
- Verification is manual, not an external identity-verification service.
- The homepage uses illustrative profiles; no demo members are seeded into production.
- The application does not transfer investment funds between members.
- Live payment collection stays disabled until Stripe is configured.

## Licensing

No project-wide open-source license has been selected. Public source availability does not itself grant an open-source license. Included third-party components retain their distributed notices, including those under `vendor/` and `scripts/vite/`.

projects.readme:
# Web App — Godtech

> **Repository category:** Location-based web application

**A location-based spiritual pilgrimage experience that helps people build a lasting practice through sacred-place discovery, prayer offerings, verified visits, and gentle gamification.**

![Godtech pilgrimage map and sanctuary discovery interface](docs/godtech-preview.png)

## Vision

Godtech explores how thoughtful technology can help people return to prayer, reflection, gratitude, and service. The experience is designed for pilgrims and spiritual seekers across traditions. It brings temples, churches, mosques, and other places of worship into one respectful discovery layer while keeping each visit centered on reverence rather than competition.

The product loop is simple:

1. Discover a nearby sacred place on the map.
2. Travel there in person.
3. Choose an intention and make a prayer offering.
4. Check in within the sanctuary's verification radius.
5. Capture a current photo as proof of the visit.
6. Earn light, maintain a devotion streak, and deepen a long-term spiritual journey.

## Current experience

- **Sacred-place discovery** — reads nearby `amenity=place_of_worship` records from OpenStreetMap through the Overpass API.
- **Multi-faith map markers** — recognizes Hindu, Buddhist, Christian, Muslim, Jewish, Sikh, and general sacred places.
- **Place imagery** — displays Wikimedia Commons imagery when the map record provides an `image` or `wikimedia_commons` tag.
- **Location-aware check-ins** — compares the visitor's current coordinates with the selected sanctuary and requires the visitor to be within 250 meters.
- **Prayer offerings** — lets pilgrims dedicate a visit to gratitude, healing, or guidance.
- **Photo proof** — opens the device camera or photo picker and requires a fresh image before a visit can be completed.
- **Pilgrim progression** — rewards verified visits with light points and presents streaks, levels, and progress toward becoming a Devotee.
- **Directions** — opens turn-by-turn directions to the selected sacred place.
- **Responsive design** — provides a map-first desktop layout and a compact, touch-friendly mobile experience.
- **Graceful fallback** — supplies sample sanctuaries when location permission or live map data is unavailable.

## Design direction

Godtech uses a calm spiritual daylight palette rather than a heavy game interface:

- warm ivory for peace and clarity;
- temple gold for devotion and earned progress;
- sacred green for presence and successful verification;
- lotus rose and soft violet for prayer categories and icon backgrounds;
- rounded, clean icon tiles that remain readable on mobile;
- a softened map treatment that keeps sacred-place markers visually prominent.

The interface borrows the immediacy of location-based exploration games while avoiding combative language, scarcity mechanics, or rankings between faiths.

## How verification works

The prototype asks for location only when it needs to center the map or verify a check-in. A pilgrimage is completed when all three conditions are satisfied:

- the pilgrim is within **250 meters** of the selected place;
- a prayer intention has been selected;
- a photo has been captured or chosen on the device.

Current progress and visit metadata are stored in the browser on the pilgrim's device. The photo preview is held only for the active session and is not uploaded to a server in this prototype.

> Production verification should use authenticated accounts, server-side distance validation, durable encrypted photo storage, consent and retention controls, moderation, duplicate-image detection, timestamp checks, and a humane appeal process. GPS and a single image can discourage casual cheating, but they cannot prove physical presence with certainty.

## Technology

| Area | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Interface | Semantic HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript |
| Map | Leaflet |
| Map tiles and places | OpenStreetMap |
| Place search | Overpass API |
| Place photos | Wikimedia Commons links supplied by map records |
| Device capabilities | Browser Geolocation and File/Camera APIs |
| Prototype state | `localStorage` |
| Hosting | OpenAI Sites configuration included in `.openai/hosting.json` |

## Run locally

No build step is required.

```bash
cd dist
python -m http.server 8765
```

Open `http://localhost:8765` in a browser. Location and camera behavior work best in a secure browser context. `localhost` is treated as secure by modern browsers.

## Project structure

```text
Web-App-Godtech/
├── .openai/
│   └── hosting.json       # Sites hosting configuration
├── dist/
│   └── index.html         # Complete application
├── docs/
│   └── godtech-preview.png
├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## Responsible product principles

- **Respect every tradition.** Sacred places are presented without ranking one faith above another.
- **Reward consistency, not compulsion.** Streaks should encourage a healthy rhythm and allow rest, travel, illness, and observance differences.
- **Protect sacred spaces.** The app should support venue-specific photography rules and never encourage disruptive behavior.
- **Minimize sensitive data.** Precise location and prayer photos require explicit purpose, short retention, strong access controls, and clear deletion tools.
- **Keep prayer sincere.** Points support the habit; they are not a measure of spiritual worth.
- **Design for safety.** Pilgrims should receive travel, accessibility, opening-hour, and local guidance before visiting unfamiliar places.

## Roadmap

- Account-based pilgrim profiles and cross-device progress
- Durable visit records with encrypted photo evidence
- Server-side geofence and anti-replay validation
- Community-maintained sanctuary pages and photography policies
- Daily, weekly, and monthly devotion journeys
- Wisdom journal and teachings curated with faith advisors
- Accessibility, opening hours, events, and trusted venue contacts
- Private groups for families, congregations, and pilgrimage circles
- Moderation, reporting, consent, retention, and deletion workflows
- Native mobile apps with more reliable camera and location attestation

## Status

Godtech is an interactive product prototype. Its discovery, map, directions, prayer-selection, location-check, photo-selection, and progression flows are functional in the browser. Authentication, cloud photo storage, automated image validation, moderation, and production-grade anti-cheat controls are planned work.

## Contributing

Ideas and contributions are welcome, especially from faith leaders, privacy engineers, accessibility specialists, cartographers, and community safety practitioners. Please approach new features with respect for religious differences and the privacy of visitors and places of worship.

## Data attribution

Map data is © [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). Place images, when available, are resolved from Wikimedia Commons references present in individual OpenStreetMap records and remain subject to their source licenses.

## License

No open-source license has been selected yet. All rights are reserved by the repository owner unless a license is added later.
